az_dry_creek_road_area.blurb: The Dry Creek Road Area covers the westernmost part of Sedona, with climbing spread through a string of canyons and formations north of the highway, among them Boynton Canyon, Fay Canyon, Long Canyon, Bear Mountain and The Fin. It is almost entirely trad, with many multi-pitch lines. Grades concentrate in 5.10 and 5.11, with a fair number of 5.9s, a tail of 5.12s and a few 5.13s, and very little below 5.9. Fay Canyon has several highly rated 5.11 to 5.12 trad lines. Boynton Canyon is an enormous canyon with towering walls, but its routes are rarely climbed, so the rock can be loose and chossy.

az_volunteer_canyon_the_cwm.blurb: Volunteer Canyon, also called The Cwm, is a remote basalt canyon in the Sycamore Canyon area of Northern Arizona. The rock is columnar basalt, among the tallest columns in the region, and the feel is rough: blocky, often loose and dirty. Climbing is almost all trad, with only a few sport routes, and grades run from 5.7 to 5.13 with most routes between 5.10 and 5.12, so moderates are scarce. Many routes start with a rappel to a belay ledge. The South Side holds the most climbs, and several of its walls face northwest and stay shaded until early afternoon or later in midsummer. The North Side has striking column lines whose routes are often sunny. Wind is common.

az_winslow_wall.blurb: Winslow Wall is a crag in East Clear Creek canyon, south of Winslow in Northern Arizona, in a secluded canyon with steep sandstone walls. The rock is Coconino sandstone, mostly very good, often with a dark patina. Sport routes dominate and are steep and technical, with patina crimps, face climbing and scoops that call for stemming, while the trad lines are steep splitter cracks. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.14, with most routes in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The East Side holds the most climbs. Prime season runs from late spring through mid-fall, since spring water is often too high and late fall can be cold. On the hottest days, chasing shade helps.

ca_echo_rock.blurb: Echo Rock is one formation in a cluster of formations and granite corridors in the central part of Joshua Tree National Park, northeast of Hidden Valley. The wider area is described as having moderate lines with a good assortment of face and crack climbing. The West Face is a large slabby face with many slab routes, mostly 5.10 and easier and mostly bolted, though not sport routes in the usual sense. Overall the climbing is trad-heavy, with some top-rope, sport and boulder problems. Grades center on 5.10, with a good number of easier climbs and a few at 5.11 and 5.12. The South Face is a small, sheltered and sunny sector. The West, East and South Faces hold the most climbs.

mt_homestake_pass.blurb: Homestake Pass lies along I-90 about seven miles east of Butte, Montana, where boulders and small crags are scattered over the pass and more remain undeveloped. The rock is coarse, solid granite. Bouldering makes up about half the climbs, with trad next and a smaller amount of sport and top-rope, and the roped climbs are up to two pitches. Problems run from V0 into the upper grades, and roped grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, with most between 5.8 and 5.10. The Tracks Bouldering, The Glen and Spaghetti Western Boulders lean toward bouldering, while Little Fire Canyon and Dragon's Back lean toward trad and sport.

nv_north_side.blurb: North Side lies on the north side of Mount Potosi in Southern Nevada and is made up of a few crags with mostly moderate routes. It is almost entirely sport, with a couple of top-rope lines. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the 5.8 to 5.10 range holding the most routes and only a thin top end. The crags include both north- and south-facing walls above 5,000 feet, which makes climbing possible on all but the hottest days of the year. Comedy Crags holds the most climbs: two roadside crags on limestone, known for how sharp the rock is, and suited to a day of cragging. Cactus Joe's is a small south-facing sport crag that gets sun all day.
